preamble: The voiceless bilabial plosive /p/ can undergo a phonetic transformation to a glottal stop /ʔ/, a process often associated with weakening or debuccalization, particularly in coda positions. While less frequent than the glottalization of /t/, this shift is attested in various languages and dialects.

examples.note: Coda /p/ can undergo glottalization, sometimes resulting in a full glottal stop, though this is less frequent than for /t/.
Final stops of Middle Chinese merged into a glottal stop in Wu and Jin; Cantonese keeps -p -t -k.
